entities.name: Query protein 768 aa
observations: Sequence length is 768 aa; estimated molecular mass is 84.15 kDa; theoretical pI is 5.83; predicted charge at pH 7 is approximately -10.3.
Sequence has Pfam PPDK_N domains across residues 99–434 and PEP-utilizers/PPE-utilizers_C domains across residues 503–768.
The sequence is 100% identical over the full query length to reviewed Flaveria bidentis chloroplastic pyruvate phosphate dikinase Q39735 in the available homology search.
The sequence is 99.5% identical to reviewed Flaveria trinervia chloroplastic pyruvate phosphate dikinase P22221.

Homology supports pyruvate phosphate dikinase activity, chloroplast localization, Mg2+ dependence, and homotetrameric assembly; these are transferred annotations rather than direct experimental evidence for the unnamed query.
The query lacks the approximately 180 aa C-terminal region present in the 953 aa reference chain, consistent with a truncated sequence or incomplete translated record.

The N-terminus is rich in Lys/Arg and contains low-complexity, Pro/Ser-rich segments, consistent with a targeting or regulatory extension, but a chloroplast transit peptide cannot be assigned with certainty from this sequence alone.

source_tools.relevance: Sequence properties, Pfam domains, and homology-based functional annotations

entities.name: Pyruvate phosphate dikinase
observations: Catalyzes pyruvate + phosphate + ATP → phosphoenolpyruvate + AMP + diphosphate + H+; EC 2.7.9.1; Rhea RHEA:10756.
Plant PPDK is associated with C4 and some CAM photosynthetic carbon fixation, where phosphoenolpyruvate is the primary CO2 acceptor.
Reference annotations report Mg2+ as a cofactor, chloroplast localization, and homotetrameric assembly.

Reference PPDK proteins contain a regulatory phosphorylation site involving a phosphothreonine near the central catalytic histidine region; plant PPDK is activated by light-induced dephosphorylation and inhibited by dark-induced phosphorylation.

source_tools.relevance: Reviewed Swiss-Prot homolog annotations and reaction mapping
